extensions.source: Shipped Svelte build: src/styles/tokens.css (tokens and derivations), src/styles/components.css (component styles ported from the reviewed prototype), src/styles/base.css, src/lib/obr/theme.ts (OBR.theme to --obr-* mapping), src/lib/obr/mock.ts (dark theme as measured, light approximated). Measured values: docs/spikes.md. Dev-harness chrome (simulated room and map) is excluded.
extensions.reviewDisposition: ship. A fresh full finish review on 2026-10-23 covered the whole surface after all user revisions; its six material fixes (own-result toast, range kept whole on wrap, GM save label and growing save button, edit-mode AC field, death-save Heal button, full-width sidebar under 460px) were applied and scored resolved.

obrThemeMapping.note: applyTheme() writes OBR.theme into the --obr-* custom properties and sets data-mode; every neutral and accent token is derived from them with color-mix(in srgb, ...). Dark defaults measured in a live room (docs/spikes.md); light values are unmeasured approximations.

light.note: Approximation: OBR's light theme has not been measured in a live room.

extensions.outOfSystem: The token-linking highlight on the map belongs to OBR's scene. The prototype simulates it with a pulsing dashed accent outline (linkPulse, 1.6s); it is prototype chrome, not a system token.

narrative.overview:
The Codex is the category-standard 5e sheet (header card, HP bar, a six-cell ability strip, tabs, dense rows) built so it could pass for a panel Owlbear Rodeo shipped itself. It takes its neutrals and its one accent from the room's theme, sets everything in OBR's own UI face, and keeps the shape language MUI-like: rounded translucent panels on Owlbear's own blurred popover paper, hairline dividers, and a solid lifted layer with a soft shadow only on things that float. Its distinction is not costume but precision: aligned tabular numerals, rows that roll everything in one click, and a roll card that anyone at the table can read without having pressed the button.

Density is high and calm. The popover is a 500px column (780px in wide mode, which gives the two-column Main tab more room) over a live map, widening by a 340px table-rolls sidebar when the user opens it. The sheet reads in layers of tone rather than borders: a transparent ground through which Owlbear's blurred paper and the map glow, then raised paper and a slightly stronger fill for controls, both thin washes of the text colour, with lists, strips and grids divided by soft hairlines. Colour does almost no decorative work. The accent marks selection, live state and primary actions; red, amber and green mean only what they mean in play.

The system explicitly rejects the parchment-and-serif fantasy costume and novelty worlds, including this project's own earlier iron-and-blood skin.
keyCharacteristics: Theme-derived: every neutral and the accent are computed from `OBR.theme` at runtime with `color-mix()`, dark and light.
One family (Roboto), weights 400/500/700, tabular numerals on every number that changes.

Overlay layering: a transparent ground under paper and control fill that are washes of the text colour; list rows and strip cells divided by soft hairlines; a solid lifted fill and shadows only on floating layers.
One accent for selection, live state and primary actions; semantic colours reserved for HP, damage and save outcomes.
Drawn SVG icons at a single 2px stroke, 16 or 18px.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: Nothing neutral and nothing accented is a fixed colour. `OBR.theme.getTheme()` is written into eight room values at runtime (`background.default` to `obr-bg`, `background.paper` to `obr-paper`, `text.primary` to `text`, `text.secondary` to `text-2`, `primary.main` to `accent`, `primary.light` and `primary.dark` to the accent-ink sources, `primary.contrastText` to `on-accent`), and every other neutral is a CSS `color-mix()` of those. The frontmatter values are the results for OBR's real dark theme, measured in a live room. The light set (sidecar `themeModes.light`) is still an approximation, unmeasured, and must be verified in a live room before it is trusted. Only the semantic hues are fixed.

rules.name: The Semantic Hues Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and green are reserved for game state: damage and HP loss, natural 1 and failure (red); half HP (amber); healthy HP and a passed save (green). They are never decoration, and they are never identity.

rules.name: The Identity Off-Hue Rule
rules.body: Identity colours (player and GM avatars on roll cards, token rings) stay off the red, amber and green hues, so an avatar can never be mistaken for a result. The shipped identity set: blue #3d8bfd, magenta #c25bb5, cyan #2b9fc0, violet #8a7cf0, orchid #d06bd9 and a second blue #4f8ff7.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent marks selection, live state and the primary action, and nothing else. Hover and pressed states are a wash of it, not a fill.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes or lines up (HP, modifiers, totals, dice breakdowns, quantities, weights, slot counts) is set with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Label Is a Header Rule
rules.body: Uppercase 11px labels name the group or column directly below them. They are never decorative tags above a heading.

rules.name: The Never-By-Itself Rule
rules.body: Nothing opens, widens or resizes the popover except the user's own click. A roll arriving bumps the unread badge and flashes the toggle; a save asked of the active sheet while the sidebar is closed raises a toast with a Show action, and so does your own roll's result ("Rapier: 20 to hit · 10 piercing"), once Dice+ has settled.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Cards, strips and rows are flat. A shadow means the layer floats, and it is always soft and diffuse.

rules.name: The Solid Float Rule
rules.body: A layer that sits over the sheet is opaque (the lifted float), never a translucent wash, so the content beneath cannot bleed through it. Everything in the sheet's own flow stays a wash, so the map shows through it.

rules.name: The One Target Row Rule
rules.body: A row is one roll target. Clicking it rolls everything the row describes (to-hit, damage and the save DC on the card), and its effects are written under the name, never split into separate per-number buttons.

rules.name: The Two Counters Rule
rules.body: Uses are circles and spell slots are squares. A counter's shape says what it counts, and the two never share a silhouette.

dos: Do derive every neutral and the accent from the room's `OBR.theme` values with `color-mix()`, so a custom palette carries through; verify the light approximations in a live room.
Do separate surfaces by tone (transparent ground, then paper and paper-2 washes of the text colour) and 1px hairlines before reaching for borders or shadows.
Do give every layer that floats over the sheet the opaque lifted float, never a translucent wash.
Do set every changing number in tabular Roboto, and size results by importance (28, 26 and 22px at 700).
Do keep roll targets at least 32px tall and make the whole row the primary roll action, rolling everything it describes.
Do divide list rows, strip cells and grid cells with 1px soft hairlines (line-soft) and keep the paper wash for hover and the open row.
Do use the accent for selection, live state and primary actions only, and the accent wash for hover and pressed states.
Do draw icons as inline SVG with a 2px round stroke at 16 or 18px.
Do draw spell slots as 14px rounded squares and uses as circles.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing animation and transitions.
donts: Don't use red, amber or green for anything but state: HP, damage, natural 1, save outcomes, warnings and connection status.
Don't give avatars or token rings a red, amber or green identity colour.
Don't put shadows on cards, rows or strips; shadows belong to floating layers, and they are always soft.
Don't introduce a second typeface, a serif, or parchment textures; the sheet should look like part of Owlbear Rodeo, not a fantasy prop.
Don't set body text in the quiet stroke tone (text-3).
Don't paint an opaque ground on the sheet inside Owlbear, or hard-code a neutral hex; the room's blurred paper is the ground and every neutral comes from the theme.
Don't auto-open the table-rolls sidebar or resize the popover when a roll arrives.
Don't split a row's to-hit, damage or save DC into separate roll buttons; the effects line is text, the row is the target.
Don't open editors as full-height panels; editing expands in place under the row.
Don't box abilities, coins or saves as separate cards; they are cells in one strip or grid, divided by soft hairlines.
